A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ViBiDSampler work, including complete main text, references, and Appendices A and B. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison; pages 3–16 render identically.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAVIS and Pexels evaluations, computational timings, and guidance ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–3, with additional qualitative results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments, timing measurements, ablations, and qualitative results, including those in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The sequential forward/backward sampling, intervening re-noising, DDS guidance, and CFG++ updates are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix A's vanilla Algorithm 2 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same DAVIS and Pexels video coverage, identical and dynamic boundary conditions in Section 4.5, and qualitative examples in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FILM, TRF, DynamiCrafter, and Generative Inbetweening. Table 2 retains the same three diffusion-based comparators, and the main-text and appendix qualitative comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains 100 DAVIS videos, 45 Pexels videos, 25-frame reference clips, 25 sampling steps per direction, and the same SVD settings and RTX 3090 hardware. Evaluation metrics and guidance-scale settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 1 and Figure 5, CFG++ scale analysis in Table 3 and Figure 6, and boundary-condition examples in Figure 7 are identical. Appendix B's qualitative comparisons are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and all qualitative result figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Ours (Full) DAVIS LPIPS 0.2355, FID 35.659, and FVD 399.15; Table 2 retains its 195-second inference time.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the DDS/Krylov-subspace optimization formulation, and accompanying mathematical reasoning are identical. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about bidirectional sampling, mitigation of off-manifold issues, training-free interpolation, and state-of-the-art quality and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of fusion artifacts, guidance benefits, motion consistency, identity preservation, and applicability to identical or dynamic bounds are unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the project-page destination from vibid.github.io to vibidsampler.github.io. Implementation details and other access information remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. Positioning relative to TRF, Generative Inbetweening, and other interpolation methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 simplifies the departmental affiliations to KAIST, removes affiliation superscripts, adds an explicit equal-contribution footnote, and updates the arXiv version/date label. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page has small placement and spacing adjustments around Figure 1 and the abstract, together with the added equal-contribution footnote. Figure content and table structures are unchanged, and pages 3–16 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revision is limited to author information, an equal-contribution note, the project-page address, and minor first-page layout adjustments. Scientific content and evidence, including both appendices, are unchanged. These edits produce no meaningful net difference in paper quality; the PDFs do not demonstrate improved resource availability.
